title: O Thou, at Whose Dread Name We Bend
description: O Thou, at Whose Dread Name We Bend in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Sprague wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 987 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For the Blessing of Schools”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou, at whose dread name we bend, To whom our pu-rest vows we pay, God o-ver all, in love de-scend, And bless the la-bors of this day.

lines: O Thou, at whose dread name we bend,
To whom our purest vows we pay,
God over all, in love descend,
And bless the labors of this day.
Our fathers here, a pilgrim band,
Fixed the proud empire of the free;
Art moved in gladness o'er the land,
And Faith her altars reared to thee.
Here, too, to guard, through every age,
The sacred rights their valor won,
They bade instruction spread her page,
And send down truth from sire to son.
Here still, through all succeeding time,
Their stores may truth and learning bring
To thee from children's children sing.

licence: Public domain: Charles Sprague died in 1875.
credits: Words by Charles Sprague (1791–1875), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
